poem.stanza:

16Listen to it closely;

poem.title: Parade
poem.stanza:
28Seven ladies
29and seventeen gentlemen
30at the Elks Club Lounge
31planning planning a parade:
32Grand Marshal in his white suit
33will lead it.
34Cadilacs with dignitaries
35will precede it.
36And behind will come
37with band and drum
38on foot... on foot...
39on foot...

40Motorcycle cops,
41white,
42will speed it
43out of sight
44if they can;
45Solid black,
46can't be right.

47Marching... marching...
48marching...
49noon till night...

50 I never knew
51 that many Negroes
52were on earth,
53did you?

poem.title: Children's Rhymes
poem.stanza:
61When I was a chile we used to play,
62 One-two-buckle my shoe!
63and things like that. But now, Lord,
64listen at them little varmints!

70There is two thousand children
71in this block, I do believe!

72 What don't bug
73then white kids
74sure bugs me;
75We knows everybody
76ain't free!

77Some of these young ones us cert'ly bad-
78One batted a hard ball right through my window
79and my gold fish et the glass.

80 What's written down
81 for white folks
82ain't for us a-tall;
83
Liberty And Justice-
84
Huh-For All.

poem.title: Sister
poem.stanza:
90That little Negro's married and got a kid.
91Why does he keep on foolin' around Marie?
92Marie's my sister-not married to me-
93But why does he keep on foolin' around Marie?
94Why don't she get a boy-friend
95I can understand-some decent man?

stanza.format: Did it ever occur to you, son,
the reason Marie runs around with trash

poem.stanza: 99Don't decent folks have dough?
101Well, anyway, it don't have to be a married man.

stanza.format: Did it ever occur to you, boy,
that a woman does the best she can?

poem.title: Preference
poem.stanza:
106I likes a woman
107six or eight and ten years older'n myself.
108I don't fool with these young girls.
109Young girl'll say,
110 Daddy, I want so-and-so.
111 I needs this, that, and the other.
112But a old woman'll say,
113 Honey, what does YOU need?
114 I just drawed my money tonight
115 and it's all your'n
116That's why I likes a older woman
117who can appreciate me:
118When she conversations you
119it ain't forever, Gimme!

poem.title: Necessity
poem.stanza:
120Work?
121I don't have to work.
122I don't have to do nothing
123but eat, drink, stay black, and die.
124This little old furnished room's
125so small I can't whip a cat
126without getting fur in my mouth
127and my landlady's so old
128her features us all run together
129and God knows she sure can overcharge-
130Which is why I reckon I does
131have to work after all.

stanza.format: Said the lady, Can you do
what my other man can't do-

poem.title: Buddy
poem.stanza:
139That kid's my buddy,
140still and yet
141I don't see him much.
142He works downtown for Twelve a week.
143Has to give his mother Ten-
144she says he can have
145the other Two
146to pay his carfare, buy a suit,
147coat, shoes,
148anything he wants out of it.

poem.title: Juke Box Love Song
poem.stanza:
149I could take the Harlem night
150and wrap around you,
151Take the neon lights and make a crown,
152Take the Lenox Avenue busses,
153Taxis, subways,
154And for your love song tone their rumble down.
155Take Harlem's heartbeat,
156Make a drumbeat,
157Put it on a record, let it whirl,
158And while we listen to it play,
159Dance with you till day-
160Dance with you, my sweet brown Harlem girl.

poem.title: Ultimatum
poem.stanza:
161Baby, how come you can't see me
162when I'm paying your bills
163each and every week?

164If you got somebody else,
165tell me-
166else I'll cut you off
167without your rent,
168I mean
169without a cent.

stanza.format: Even if it is my home.

poem.title: Not a Movie
poem.stanza:
218Well, they rocked him with road-apples
219because he tried to vote
220and whipped his head with clubs
221and he crawled on his knees to his house
222and he got the midnight train
223and he crossed that Dixie line
224now he's livin'
225on a 133rd.

226He didn't stop in Washington
227and he didn't stop in Baltimore
228neither in Newark on the way.
229Six knots was on his head
230but, thank God, he wasn'r dead!
231And there ain't no Ku Klux
232on a 133rd

poem.stanza:
249If I ever hit for a dollar

252I ain't gonna
253play back a cent.

254(Of course, I might
255combinatea little

258pregnant again!

259Fate must have

262cullud nation!

poem.title: Motto
poem.stanza:
268I play it cool
269And dig all jive.
270That's the reason
271I stay alive.

272My motto,
273As I live and learn,
274 is:
275 Dig and Be Dug
276 In Return

poem.title: Dead in There
poem.stanza:
277Sometimes
278A night funeral
279Going by
280Carries home
281A cool bop daddy.

282Hearse and flowers
283Guarantee
284He'll never hype
285Another paddy.

286It's hard to believe,
287But dead in there,
288He'll never lay a
289Hype nowhere!

290He's my ace-boy,
291Gone away.
292 Wake up and live!
293He used to say.

294Squares
295Who couldn't dig him,
296Plant him now--
297Out where it makes
298No diff' no how.

poem.title: Situation
poem.stanza:
299When I rolled three 7's
300in a row
301I was scared to walk out
302with the dough.

poem.title: Dancer
poem.stanza:
303Two or three things in the past
304failed him
305that had not failed people
306of lesser genius.

307In the first place
308he didn't have much sense.
309He was no good at making love
310and no good at making money.
311So he tapped,
312 trucked,
313 boogied,
314 sanded,
315 jittered,
316until he made folks say,
317 Looky yonder
318 at that boy!
319 Hey!
320But being no good at lovin'--
321the girls left him.
322(When you're no good for dough they go.)
323With no sense, just wonderful feet,
324What could possibly be all-reet?
325Did he get anywhere? No!

326Even a great dancer
327can't C.P.T.
328a show.

poem.title: Advice
poem.stanza:
329Folks, I'm telling you,
330birthing is hard
331and dying is mean--
332so get yourself
333a little loving
334in between.

poem.title: Green Memory
poem.stanza:
335A wonderful time--the War:
336when money rolled in
337and blood rolled out.
338 But blood
339 was far away
340 from here--
341Money was near.

poem.title: Wine-O
poem.stanza:
342Setting in the wine-house
343Soaking up a wine-souse
344Waiting for tomorrow to come--
345Then
346Setting in the wine-house
347Soaking up a new souse.
348Tomorrow...
349Oh, hum!

poem.title: Relief
poem.stanza:
350My heart is aching
351for them Poles and Greeks
352on relief way across the sea
353because I was on relief
354once in 1933

355I know what relief can be--
356it took me two years to get on WPA.
357If the war hadn't come along
358I wouldn't be out the barrel yet.
359Now, I'm almost back in the barrel again.

360To tell the truth,
361if these white folks want to go ahead
362and fight another war,
363or even two,
364the one to stop 'em won't be me.
365Would you?

poem.title: Ballad of the Landlord
poem.stanza:
366Landlord, landlord,
367My roof has sprung a leak.
368Don't you 'member I told you about it
369Way last week?

370Landlord, landlord
371These steps is broken down.
372When you come up yourself
373It's a wonder you don't fall down

374Ten Bucks you say I owe you?
375Ten Bucks you say is due?
376Well, that's Ten Bucks more'n I'll pay you
377Till you fix this house up new.

378What? You gonna get eviction orders?
379You gonna cut off my heat?
380You gonna take my furniture and
381Throw it in the street?

382Um-huh! You talking high and mighty.
383Talk on--till you get through.
384You ain't gonna be able to say a word
385If I land my fist on you.

stanza.format: He's trying to ruin the government

poem.stanza:
390Copper's whistle!
391Patrol Bell!
392Arrest.

393Precinct Station.

407On the day when the Savoy

413St. James Presbyterian
414and 409 Edgecombe

417Do, Jesus!
418Manhattan Island will whirl
419like a Dizzy Gillespie transcription
420played by Inez and Timmie.
421On that day, Lord,
422Sammy Davis and Marian Anderson

424Paul Robeson

poem.title: Flatted Fifths
poem.stanza:
430Little cullud boys with beards
431re-bop be-bop mop and stop

432Little cullud boys with fears,
433frantic, kick their draftee years
434into flatted and flatter beers
435that at a sudden change become
436sparkling Oriental wines
437rich and strange
438silken bathrobes with gold twines
439and Heilbroner, Crawford,
440Nat-undreamed-of Lewis combines
441in silver thread and diamond notes
442on trade-marks inside
443Howard coats

444Little cullud boys in berets
445 oop pop-a-da
446horse a fantasy of days
447 ool ya koo
448and dig all plays.

453cigarette machine

poem.title: Shame on You
poem.stanza:
495If you're great enough
496and clever enough
497the government might honor you.
498But the people will forget --
499Except on holidays.

500A movie house in Harlem named after Lincoln,
501Nothing at all named after John Brown.

502Black people don't remember
503any better than white

504If you're not alive and kicking,
505 shame on you!

507 Oh, my, my!
508What a grand time was the war!
509 My, my, my!
510In wartime we had fun,
511Sorry that old war is done!
512What a grand time was the war,
513 My, my!

514Echo:
515 Did
516 Somebody

poem.title: Mystery
poem.stanza:
518When a chile gets to be thirteen
519and ain't seen Christ yet,
520she needs to set on de moaner's bench
521night and day.

522 Jesus, lover of my soul!
523Hail, Mary, mother of God!
524 Let me to thy bosom fly!
525Amen! Hallelujah!

stanza.format: Coming for to carry me home.

poem.stanza:
528Sunday morning where the rhythm flows,
529how old nobody knows --
530yet old as mystery,
531older than creed,
532basic and wondering
533and lost as my need.

538Father, Bishop, Effendi, Mother Horne.

546When pimps out of loneliness cry:

551 My God!

poem.title: Testimonial
poem.stanza:
554If I just had a piano,
555if I just had a organ,
556if I just had a drum,
557how I could praise my Lord!

558But I don't need no piano,
559 neither organ
560 nor drum
561for to praise my Lord

poem.title: Passing
poem.stanza:
562On sunny summer Sunday afternoons in Harlem
563when the air is one interminable ball game
564and grandma cannot get her gospel hymns
565from the Saints of God in Christ
566on account of the Dodgers on the radio,

567on sunny Sunday afternoons
568when the kids look all new
569and far too clean to stay that way,
570and Harlem has its
571washed-and-ironed-and-cleaned-best out,
572the ones who've crossed the line
573to live downtown
574miss you,
575Harlem of the bitter dream
576since their dream has
577come true.

poem.title: Sunday by the Combination
poem.stanza:
590I feel like dancin', baby,
591till the sun goes down.

592But I wonder where
593the sunrise
594Monday morning's gonna be?

595I feel like dancin'!
596Baby, dance with me!

597He was a soldier in the army,
598But he doesn't walk like one.
599He walks like his soldiering *
600Days are done.
601Son! ... Son!

poem.title: Night Funeral in Harlem
poem.stanza:
606Insurance man, he did not pay --
607His insurance lapsed the other day --

608Yet they got a satin box
609For his head to lay.

614Them flowers came
615from that poor boy's friends-
616They'll want flowers, too,
617When they meet their ends.

622Old preacher-man
623Preached that boy away-
624Charged Five Dollars
625His girl friend had to pay.

628When it was all over
629And the lid shut on his head
630and the organ had done played
631and the last prayers been said
632and six pallbearers

633Carried him out for dead
634And off down Lenox Avenue
635That long black hearse done sped,
636 The streetlight
637 At his corner
638 Shined just like a tear-
639That boy that they was mournin'
640Was so dear, so dear
641To them folks that brought the flowers,
642To that girl who paid the preacher man-
643It was all their tears that made
644 That poor boy's
645 Funeral grand.
646 Night funeral
647 In Harlem.

poem.title: Blues at Dawn
poem.stanza:
648I don't dare start thinking in the morning.
649I don't dare start thinking in the morning.
650 If I thought thoughts in bed,
651 Them thoughts would bust my head-
652So I don't dare start thinking in the morning.

653I don't dare remember in the morning
654Don't dare remember in the morning.
655 If I recall the day before,
656 I wouldn't get up no more-
657So I don't dare remember in the morning.

poem.title: Dime
poem.stanza: 658Chile, these steps is hard to climb.
660Montage of a dream deferred:
663Chile, Granny ain't got no dime.

666White is right,
667Yellow mellow,

poem.title: Neighbor
poem.stanza:
676Down home
677he sets on a stoop
678and watches the sun go by.
679In Harlem
680when his work is done
681he sets in a bar with a beer.
682He looks taller than he is
683and younger than he ain't.
684He looks darker than he is, too.
685And he's smarter than he looks,

688Now he ain't neither.
689He's a good man,
690except he talks too much.
691In fact, he's a great cat.
692But when he drinks,
693he drinks fast.

696True,
697he just
698lets his glass
699set there.

poem.title: Evening Song
poem.stanza:
700A woman standing in the doorway
701Trying to make her where-with-all:
702 Come here, baby, darlin'!
703 Don't you hear me call?

704If I was anybody's sister,
705I'd tell her, Gimme a place to sleep.
706But I ain't nobody's sister.
707I'm just a poor lost sheep.

708Mary, Mary, Mary,
709Had a little lamb.
710Well, I hope that lamb of Mary's
711Don't turn out like I am.

poem.title: Chord
poem.stanza:
712Shadow faces
713In the shadow night
714Before the early dawn
715Bops bright.

716There's been an eagle on a nickel,
717An eagle on a quarter, too.

719On a dime.

732Mingled
733breath and smell*

poem.stanza:
739We're related-you and I,
740You from the West Indies,
741I from Kentucky.

742Kinsmen- you and I,
743You from Africa,

poem.title: Likewise
poem.stanza: 746The Jews:

747Groceries
748Suits
749Fruits
750Watches
751Diamond rings
752 THE DAILY NEWS

753Jews sell me things.
754Yom Kippur, no!
755Shops all over Harlem
756close up tight that night.

757Some folks blame high prices on the Jews.
758(Some folks blame too much on Jews.)
759But in Harlem they don't answer back,
760Just maybe shrug their shoulders,
761"What's the use?"
762What's the use
763in Harlem?
764What's the use?
765What's the Harlem?
766Use in Harlem

771Sometimes I think
772Jews have heard
773the music of a
774dream deferred.

poem.title: Silver
poem.stanza:
775Cheap little rhymes
776A cheap little tune
777Are sometimes as dangerous
778As a sliver of the moon.
779A cheap little tune
780To cheap little rhymes
781Can cut a man's
782Throat sometimes.

poem.title: Hope
poem.stanza:
783He rose up on his dying bed
784and asked for fish.
785His wife looked it up in her dream book
786and played it.

poem.title: Dream Boogie: Variation
poem.stanza:
787Tinkling treble,
788Rolling bass,
789High noon teeth
790In a midnight face,
791Great long fingers
792On great big hands,
793Screaming pedals
794Where his twelve-shoe lands,
795Looks like his eyes
796Are teasing pain,
797A few minutes late
798For the Freedom Train.

poem.title: Harlem
poem.stanza: 799What happens to a dream deffered?

800Does it dry up
801like a raisin in the sun?
802Or fester like a sore-
803And then run?
804Does it stink like rotten meat?
805Or crust and sugar over-
806like a syrupy sweet?

807Maybe it just sags
808like a heavy load.

poem.title: Good Morning
poem.stanza:
810Good morning, daddy!
811I was born here, he said,
812watched Harlem grow
813until colored folks spread
814from river to river
815across the middle of Manhatten
816out of Penn Station
817dark tenth of a nation,
818planes from Puerto Rico
819and holds of boats, chico,
820up from Cuba Haiti Jamaica
821in buses marked New York
822from Georgia Florida Louisiana
823to Harlem Brookly the Bronx
824but most of all to Harlem
825dusky sash across Manhattan
826I've seen them come dark

827wondering
828wide-eyed
829dreaming

830out of Penn Station-
831but the trains are late.
832The gates open-
833but the trains are late.
834The gates open-
835Yet there're bars
836at each gate.

837What happens
838to a dream deferred?
839Daddy, ain't you heard?

poem.title: Same in Blues
poem.stanza:
840I said to my baby,
841Baby, take it slow.
842I can't, she said, I can't!
843I got to go!

847Lulu said to leonard,
848I want a diamond ring.
849Leonard said to Lulu,
850You won't get a goddamn thing!

854Daddy, daddy, daddy,
855All I want is you.
856You can have me, baby-
857but my lovin' days is through.

861Three parties
862On my party line-
863But that third party,
864Lord, ain't mine!

868From river to river,
869Uptown and Down,
870There's liable to be confusion
871when a dream gets kicked around.

poem.title: Comment on Curb
poem.stanza:
872You talk like
873They don't kick
874dreams around
875downtown.

stanza.format: Time I pay rent and get my food
and laundry I don't have much left
but here is five dollars for you
to show you I still appreciates you.
My girl-friend send her love and say
she hopes to lay eyes on you sometime in life.
Mama, it has been raining cats and dogs up
here. Well, that is all so I will close.

poem.title: Island
poem.stanza:
891Between two rivers,
892North of the park,
893Like darker rivers
894The streets are dark.

895Black and white,
896Gold and brown-
897Chocolate-custard
898Pie of a town.
901Good morning, daddy!
